name: phase2_tier2_feasibility
description: Does the operand modulate FREQUENCY, not just power? Tiers 2 and 3 of the
receiver ladder read frequency (world-readable scaling_cur_freq) and
self-timing dilation, so both need a DVFS response to observe. Under
Config-A there is none by construction; this runs under Config-B.
The reason to doubt it: this part reports PL1 = 200 W and PL2 = 80 W,
while four victim threads draw about 16 W package and the die sits near
50 C against a Tjmax around 100. Nothing is limiting, so nothing has to
clock down, and a 1.9 W operand difference on top of that may move the
So the load is swept rather than assumed. t4 is the standard placement
(P-cores, stride 2). t10 fills the P-cores including SMT siblings. t18
adds the E-cores, which is the most package power this machine can be
made to draw from user space. If the frequency delta is still at the
noise floor at t18, tiers 2 and 3 are not reachable on this hardware at
these limits, and that is a result about the platform rather than a gap
Read the MHz column per condition, not the watts. aa_t18 is the control:
the same operand in both conditions at the highest load, so any frequency
difference it shows is drift rather than signal.

runs.label: t4
runs.comment: Standard placement: 5 P-cores at stride 2. ~16 W.

runs.label: t18
runs.comment: P-cores and E-cores: the most package power reachable from user space.

runs.label: aa_t18
runs.comment: A/A at the highest load: bounds what drift alone can produce.
